conventions: A coupling bound is not automatically a unique prediction.
excludes: A universal numerical bound on all gauge couplings
An established experimental signal from projected sensitivity

sources.title: Consistency of matter models with asymptotically safe quantum gravity

evidence.text: The gravitino calculation uses an irreducible SO(5) decomposition on a four-dimensional spherical background and local-supersymmetry gauge fixing with alpha'=0. Faddeev-Popov and Nielsen-Kallosh ghosts reduce the stated eight components to two propagating degrees of freedom.

sources.title: Viability of quantum-gravity induced ultraviolet completions for matter

evidence.text: The calculation uses a linear background-field split about flat space, York decomposition, gauge parameters α=β=0, and a spectrally/RG-adjusted Litim regulator. Trace-mode inclusion and a non-spectral regulator provide restricted approximation checks.

sources.title: Upper bound on the Abelian gauge coupling from asymptotic safety

evidence.text: Select α=0, β=1 by agreement of the three coupling extractions for the chosen regulator and perturbative approximation. Integrate hypercharge flow using imported single-metric gravitational beta functions with minimally coupled matter and ηh=0.

sources.title: Constraining power of asymptotic safety for scalar fields

evidence.text: Resolve metric modes, choose a background-covariant gauge, and consistently include its scalar-background prefactor. The reported α=β=0 limit removes one scalar metric contribution.

sources.title: Are there ALPs in the asymptotically safe landscape?

evidence.text: Use the functional RG flow k∂kΓk=(1/2)Tr[(Γk⁽²⁾+Rk)⁻¹k∂kRk], a truncation motivated by canonical power counting, and vertex projections to extract matter beta functions and anomalous dimensions. The computation uses a flat background and a Litim regulator.

evidence.text: Find fixed points numerically: simple subsystems use Mathematica NSolve, with completeness checks reported by the authors. More complicated systems first solve the matter equations at approximate gravitational fixed-point coordinates, then use those roots to initialize FindRoot for the coupled system.

sources.title: Asymptotic safety in generalized Proca theories

evidence.text: Uses the Wetterich functional RG equation and background-field method, with linear metric/vector splits, gravitational gauge fixing and Faddeev–Popov ghosts. Beta functions are extracted by matching background operators.

sources.title: On avoiding Ostrogradski instabilities within Asymptotic Safety

evidence.text: Use a Litim regulator and a distributional external-momentum expansion that retains integration-boundary contributions. The appendix adopts Θ(0) = 1/2; surface terms affect higher-order kinetic terms but not the scalar anomalous dimension.

sources.title: On avoiding Ostrogradski instabilities within Asymptotic Safety

evidence.text: Project the functional renormalization group equation for the effective average action onto the retained gravitational and scalar operators. The regulator vanishes as k → 0, where Γk becomes the ordinary effective action.

sources.title: Scalar-tensor theories within Asymptotic Safety

evidence.text: Use linear background-field splits, harmonic gauge, and a Type I regulator with Litim profile Rk(z)=(k²−z)θ(k²−z). Interaction vertices are generated using xAct; the retained projection receives contributions from 18 traces.

targets: Spectral functions, form factors and scattering ingredients
regimes: Finite FRG cutoff and the vanishing-cutoff limit

conventions: At finite cutoff, background and quantum equations of motion need not agree.

evidence.text: For Δ=−∇²+E1+E2, cutoff types I, II and III use −∇², −∇²+E1 and full Δ respectively; E2 contains couplings. Type III is spectrally adjusted. Most explicit calculations use an optimized profile.

sources.title: Further evidence for asymptotic safety of quantum gravity

evidence.text: Expand the fixed-point equation about R=0. Algebraic recursion expresses every λ_n for n≥2 as a rational function of λ_0 and λ_1. Numerically select real roots consistent across orders, reject coincident denominator zeros, and compare both coordinates and eigenvalues.

sources.title: The unitary conformal field theory behind 2D Asymptotic Safety

evidence.text: Expands the Einstein–Hilbert functional under Weyl rescalings after subtracting its Euler-characteristic pole. The finite Weyl variation is related to a Liouville/Wess–Zumino functional; Diff×Weyl invariance restricts the remaining ambiguity to moduli dependence.

evidence.text: Functional renormalisation group with transverse-traceless decomposition and early-time heat-kernel traces. Physical fluctuations retain an optimised type-I cutoff; unphysical sectors instead regulate each shifted Laplace operator Δ_i as Δ_i+R_k(Δ_i), maintaining cancellations while removing technical curvature denominators.
